/-!
# Conjecture 4.55

by K. W. Roggenkamp

Let $G$ be a finite group, and $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ the localization at $p$. Can every projective
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-module be uniquely, up to permutations and isomorphisms, written as a direct
sum of indecomposable projective $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-modules?

Here $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ is the localization of $\mathbb{Z}$ at the prime ideal $(p)$ (not the
$p$-adic completion), and $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$ is the group ring. The projective modules in the
question are arbitrary (not necessarily finitely generated), and the index set of a decomposition
may be infinite.

It is known that the category of finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-modules is
not a Krull–Schmidt category, i.e. $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$ is not always semiperfect (Woods 1974;
for example $G = C_3$ with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, see Johnston–Rumynin). Local endomorphism
rings of the indecomposable summands are sufficient, but not necessary, for unique decomposition,
so this does not answer the question, which remains open.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 4.55
- [D. Johnston, D. Rumynin, *On a question by Roggenkamp about group
  algebras*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21316), Problem 3
- S. M. Woods, *Some results on semi-perfect group rings*, Canadian J. Math. **26** (1974),
  121–129
-/

/-- The localization $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of $\mathbb{Z}$ at the prime ideal $(p)$. -/
local notation "ℤ_(" p ")" => Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)})

blocks.command_arg: {R : Type*} [Ring R] {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
blocks.text: variable {R : Type*} [Ring R] {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]

blocks.code:
def IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : ι → Submodule R P) : Prop :=
  DirectSum.IsInternal A ∧ ∀ i, Module.Projective R (A i) ∧ Indecomposable (ModuleCat.of R (A i))
blocks.docstring:
A family `A` of submodules of an `R`-module `P`, indexed by `ι`, is a decomposition of `P`
into indecomposable projective modules if `P` is the internal direct sum $\bigoplus_i A_i$
and every $A_i$ is an indecomposable projective `R`-module.

justification.closest_existing_considered: DirectSum.IsInternal (used inside), CategoryTheory.Indecomposable on ModuleCat (used inside; Mathlib has no module-level `Module.Indecomposable`), DirectSum.Decomposition (a data-carrying structure, not a Prop about a family of submodules, and it does not include indecomposability/projectivity of summands).
justification.name: Kourovka.«4.55».IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition
justification.why_needed: Bundles the condition 'A : ι → Submodule R P is an internal direct-sum decomposition (DirectSum.IsInternal A) and each A i is a projective and indecomposable R-module' which is used three times (once for existence, twice for uniqueness). It is built only from Mathlib primitives: DirectSum.IsInternal, Module.Projective, and CategoryTheory.Indecomposable applied to ModuleCat.of R (A i). An API lemma (empty decomposition of the zero module) is included and proved.

blocks.name: IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition
blocks.text:
/-- A family `A` of submodules of an `R`-module `P`, indexed by `ι`, is a decomposition of `P`
into indecomposable projective modules if `P` is the internal direct sum $\bigoplus_i A_i$
and every $A_i$ is an indecomposable projective `R`-module. -/
def IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : ι → Submodule R P) : Prop :=
  DirectSum.IsInternal A ∧ ∀ i, Module.Projective R (A i) ∧ Indecomposable (ModuleCat.of R (A i))

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 16]
theorem isIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition_empty [Subsingleton P] :
    IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition (fun _ : Empty => (⊥ : Submodule R P)) :=
  ⟨⟨fun _ _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun _ => ⟨0, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩⟩, fun i => i.elim⟩
blocks.docstring:
The empty family is a decomposition of the zero module into indecomposable projective
modules.

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]
      (P : Type) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P],
      Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P →
        (∃ (ι : Type) (_ : DecidableEq ι) (A : ι → Submodule (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P),
          IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition A) ∧
        ∀ (ι κ : Type) [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq κ]
          (A : ι → Submodule (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P)
          (B : κ → Submodule (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P),
          IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition A →
          IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition B →
          ∃ e : ι ≃ κ, ∀ i, Nonempty (A i ≃ₗ[MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G] B (e i)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ the localization at $p$. Can every projective
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-module be uniquely, up to permutations and isomorphisms, written as a direct
sum of indecomposable projective $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-modules?

That is: for every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ and every projective
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-module $P$, does $P$ admit a decomposition $P = \bigoplus_{i \in I} P_i$
into indecomposable projective submodules, and given any two such decompositions
$P = \bigoplus_{i \in I} P_i = \bigoplus_{j \in J} Q_j$, is there a bijection
$e \colon I \to J$ with $P_i \cong Q_{e(i)}$ for all $i \in I$?

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question implicitly quantified over all finite groups G and all primes p; 'every projective module' means arbitrary (not necessarily finitely generated) projective Z_(p)G-modules (Johnston–Rumynin's Problem 3), and 'uniquely written' includes both existence of a decomposition into indecomposable projectives (possibly infinite index set) and uniqueness up to a bijection of summands with pairwise isomorphisms; the remark that f.g. projectives are not a Krull–Schmidt category (Woods 1974, i.e. Z_(p)G is not always semiperfect, e.g. G=C_3, p≡1 mod 3) is a stated known fact, not a posed question, and does not settle this one since unique decomposition does not require local endomorphism rings.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same content (∀ prime p, finite group G, arbitrary projective module P over MonoidAlgebra (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span {(p:ℤ)})) G: a decomposition into indecomposable projective summands exists, and any two such decompositions are matched by a bijection of index sets with pairwise linear isomorphisms), matching Johnston–Rumynin's Problem 3. c01 is the cleanest faithful version: it uses Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Indecomposable on ModuleCat (verified non-degenerate: ¬IsZero ∧ no nontrivial biproduct splitting, all in universe 0 consistent with P : Type), internal direct sums via DirectSum.IsInternal (a Prop independent of the DecidableEq instance), one small bespoke predicate with an API sanity lemma, correct references (its Johnston–Rumynin title 'On a question by Roggenkamp about group algebras' matches the arXiv source; c05/c06/c07 cite fabricated titles), and a docstring that records the Woods remark as background. Only edit: softened 'the smallest example is G = C_3' to 'for example G = C_3' in the module docstring. Restricting index types and summands to Type is WLOG since nonzero independent summands inject into P.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.55

by K. W. Roggenkamp

Let $G$ be a finite group, and $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ the localization at $p$. Can every projective
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-module be uniquely, up to permutations and isomorphisms, written as a direct
sum of indecomposable projective $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-modules?

Here $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ is the localization of $\mathbb{Z}$ at the prime ideal $(p)$ (not the

question are arbitrary (not necessarily finitely generated), and the index set of a decomposition
may be infinite.

It is known that the category of finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-modules is
not a Krull–Schmidt category, i.e. $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$ is not always semiperfect (Woods 1974;
for example $G = C_3$ with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, see Johnston–Rumynin). Local endomorphism
rings of the indecomposable summands are sufficient, but not necessary, for unique decomposition,
so this does not answer the question, which remains open.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 4.55
- [D. Johnston, D. Rumynin, *On a question by Roggenkamp about group
  algebras*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21316), Problem 3
- S. M. Woods, *Some results on semi-perfect group rings*, Canadian J. Math. **26** (1974),
  121–129
-/

open CategoryTheory

namespace Kourovka.«4.55»

/-- The localization $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of $\mathbb{Z}$ at the prime ideal $(p)$. -/
local notation "ℤ_(" p ")" => Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)})

variable {R : Type*} [Ring R] {P : Type*} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]

/-- A family `A` of submodules of an `R`-module `P`, indexed by `ι`, is a decomposition of `P`
into indecomposable projective modules if `P` is the internal direct sum $\bigoplus_i A_i$
and every $A_i$ is an indecomposable projective `R`-module. -/
def IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : ι → Submodule R P) : Prop :=
  DirectSum.IsInternal A ∧ ∀ i, Module.Projective R (A i) ∧ Indecomposable (ModuleCat.of R (A i))

/-- The empty family is a decomposition of the zero module into indecomposable projective
modules. -/
@[category API, AMS 16]
theorem isIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition_empty [Subsingleton P] :
    IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition (fun _ : Empty => (⊥ : Submodule R P)) :=
  ⟨⟨fun _ _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun _ => ⟨0, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩⟩, fun i => i.elim⟩

/--
Let $G$ be a finite group, and $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ the localization at $p$. Can every projective
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-module be uniquely, up to permutations and isomorphisms, written as a direct
sum of indecomposable projective $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-modules?

That is: for every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ and every projective
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}G$-module $P$, does $P$ admit a decomposition $P = \bigoplus_{i \in I} P_i$
into indecomposable projective submodules, and given any two such decompositions
$P = \bigoplus_{i \in I} P_i = \bigoplus_{j \in J} Q_j$, is there a bijection
$e \colon I \to J$ with $P_i \cong Q_{e(i)}$ for all $i \in I$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]
      (P : Type) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P],
      Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P →
        (∃ (ι : Type) (_ : DecidableEq ι) (A : ι → Submodule (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P),
          IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition A) ∧
        ∀ (ι κ : Type) [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq κ]
          (A : ι → Submodule (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P)
          (B : κ → Submodule (MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G) P),
          IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition A →
          IsIndecomposableProjectiveDecomposition B →
          ∃ e : ι ≃ κ, ∀ i, Nonempty (A i ≃ₗ[MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G] B (e i)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.55»

items: ℤ_(p) is modelled as `Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)})` with `[Fact p.Prime]` supplying the primality instance (via Int.ideal_span_isMaximal_of_prime); this is the localization of ℤ at (p), deliberately not the p-adic integers ℤ_[p].
The group ring ℤ_(p)G is `MonoidAlgebra ℤ_(p) G`; G is any `[Group G] [Finite G]`.

Indecomposability of a summand is `CategoryTheory.Indecomposable (ModuleCat.of R (A i))`, i.e. nonzero (not IsZero ↔ not Subsingleton) and every iso with a biproduct Y ⊞ Z has Y or Z zero. Universe: ModuleCat.{0}, consistent with P : Type.

Projectivity of the summands is included in the decomposition predicate to mirror the text 'indecomposable projective'; it is mathematically redundant (direct summands of projectives are projective) and so does not change the statement.

Decompositions are internal (families of submodules with DirectSum.IsInternal) rather than external isomorphisms P ≃ ⨁ P_i; these are equivalent, and with P : Type an index type in `Type` suffices since the nonzero independent summands inject into P.
Uniqueness 'up to permutations and isomorphisms' is: for any two decompositions indexed by ι, κ there is `e : ι ≃ κ` with `Nonempty (A i ≃ₗ[R] B (e i))` for all i.

The statement includes both existence of a decomposition into indecomposables and uniqueness, following the decomposition table and Johnston–Rumynin's Problem 3 (arbitrary, not necessarily finitely generated, projectives).

DecidableEq instances required by DirectSum.IsInternal are quantified explicitly (∃ (_ : DecidableEq ι) / ∀ [DecidableEq ι]) instead of opening Classical; this is harmless since IsInternal does not depend propositionally on the instance.
Module types are quantified over `Type` (repository convention), as are G and the index types.
AMS tags 16 (associative rings/algebras: group rings, projective modules) and 20 (group theory).

reviewer_notes: Interpretation: the question is read as Johnston–Rumynin Problem 3 (arbitrary, not necessarily finitely generated, projective ℤ_(p)G-modules; existence + uniqueness of decomposition into indecomposable projectives, possibly infinite index set), as in the decomposition table. answer(True) = positive answer. The Woods remark (f.g. projectives not Krull–Schmidt, i.e. ℤ_(p)G not always semiperfect) is a known fact, not a slot; it is recorded in the docstring only. Boundary: zero module (e.g. P = 0) has the unique empty decomposition; the file includes an API lemma checking this. Projectivity of summands is redundant (summands of projectives are projective) but kept to mirror the text. Other candidates: c02/c04 (bespoke IsIndecomposable via IsCompl submodules) and c06 (via idempotent endomorphisms) are also correct but more bespoke; c03 lacks a proper module docstring/remark; c05 has excessive universe polymorphism and wrong reference title; c07 quantifies over maximal ideals of ℤ and uses ModuleCat objects, correct but less readable, and wrong reference title. No candidate omitted the slot.
